definitions.explanation: To wind something back to an earlier position. Originally used for tape and film, now also used figuratively for going back in time or reversing progress in digital contexts.

examples.japanese: テープを{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す。
{動画|どうが}を{少|すこ}し{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}してもう{一度|いちど}{見|み}た。
examples.english: I rewound the video a little and watched it again.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}すことができたら、{違|ちが}う{選択|せんたく}をしていただろう。
examples.english: If I could turn back time, I would have made a different choice.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す is transitive.

ASPECT (ている): {巻|ま}き{戻|もど}している describes the action of rewinding in progress.

USAGE: Originally a physical action (rewinding cassette tapes, film reels), {巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す is now commonly used for digital media and figuratively for turning back time.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [tape/video/time]を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す (to rewind something)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- テープを{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す: to rewind a tape
- {時間|じかん}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す: to turn back time
- {動画|どうが}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}す: to rewind a video
